chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Showing how the hobbler grows out of the Pretty Foot
summary: Green demonstrates the Pretty Foot melting into the hobbler with How Come You Do Me Like You Do, and recites Bert Williams' song Nobody.

blocks.x: Let me ask you a question, now, Chuck. Can you do the way the Pretty Foot --
how one comes from the other? Do the Pretty Foot first and then do the hobbler -- show just how they melt together.

Yes, they intervene, you see. Like -- well he has acquainted himself -- the first partner has acquainted and the Pretty Foot is occurring. Sing that song, 'How Come you Do me like you Do, Do, Do -- I ain't nothing to you.' See, that's the Pretty Foot, see, and that be happening and --
And all the pretty girls come out and the

ladies surround the men, who says, "Who is that handsome man?" "Nobody." And when they're serving the seven-course meals, and the first chef (unintelligible) and someone says, "Is my steak in the pan?" "Nobody." Slowly they rise to pay their price. (unintelligible) "Can't you get his hand out of his pocket?" "No, mister, nobody can."
Well, that was the Ziegfield Follies star, you know. He used to be the world's greatest comedian, number one in the world. The song go, Nobody -- Bert Williams, you see. Williams and Walker.
